item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0007-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0007-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0007-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0007-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0007-E005","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"After the Federal Constitutional Court declared the transfer of Corona funds to the Climate and Transformation Fund unconstitutional, the government was compelled to prepare a supplementary 2023 budget and postponed adoption of the regular 2024 budget; 47% of respondents favored spending cuts while 35% favored suspending the debt brake by declaring another emergency.","notes":["The excerpt does not state that the transferred amount was €60 billion."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0007-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0007-E007","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"On 6 July 2023, the Bundestag passed the 11th amendment to the Competition Act, which was intended to strengthen sector investigations, improve benefit skimming and merger-notification powers, and allow remedies for serious competition disturbances up to separation; the Federal Cartel Office reported active enforcement, including energy-price-brake reviews, digital-platform cases, merger conditions, and more than 255,000 competition-register queries.","notes":["The excerpt says the Bundestag passed the amendment and describes intended or newly available powers; it does not establish that Germany had already enacted and operationally applied all of them.","The excerpt states that the competition register had been fully operational for over a year, but does not use the phrase 'fully operational' as a general characterization of all enforcement described."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0007-E008","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"On 5 July 2023, the Bundestag committee rejected the opposition's request for a federal Cum-Ex inquiry into the Warburg Bank affair and Scholz's role; SPD, Greens, and FDP members opposed it, citing concerns about constitutional competence and federalism, while the opposition argued that the coalition had not concretely substantiated its objections and that the proposed partial inquiry was unacceptable.","notes":["The excerpt says the coalition rejected the request and raised constitutional and federal-state competence concerns.","The excerpt does not support saying that the coalition rejected a narrower proposal; it says the opposition's amendment was accepted by the committee but, according to the coalition, did not cure the alleged inadmissibility."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0007-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0007-E010","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that Germany's 2022 rights conditions included high levels of politically motivated and right-wing crimes, gaps in police anti-racism training and independent complaint bodies, a fatal police shooting of a 16-year-old asylum seeker under investigation, prosecutions under Germany's universal-jurisdiction laws, limited eligibility for some Ukraine refugees, a ban on several Nakba protests upheld by courts, and climate measures judged insufficient despite stated emissions targets.","notes":["The excerpt supports an increase in politically motivated crimes from 2020 to 2021 and reports 2022 crime figures, but does not establish that politically motivated or right-wing crimes rose during 2022.","The excerpt documents universal-jurisdiction prosecutions and states that German law recognizes universal jurisdiction; it does not establish that prosecutions expanded."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0007-E011","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
